features.note: Ears read as bright metal (0.793) against the lifted charcoal chassis (0.189). No regression.

COUNTABLE BY EYE NOW. With the exposure lifted (module face 0.433 vs chassis 0.189), the row of module bays with their handles and dividers reads directly in the front-detail — no brightening needed. The exact fix I asked for landed.
PSU bank (face 0.293) separates from the module bank (0.433) at 32% Weber — the tightest pair, resolved so the two banks are distinguishable, which is what lets a viewer count them.

RJ45 reads by its metal CAGE (100% vs its own throat, the correct cue) not its bore; alarm block reads at the front-left. The cavity behind them stays 0.001 by design (a recess must read dark), asserted explicitly.

Emissive lamps use distinct colours per state (led_blue standby, led_green enabled), verified headless at 87%/92% saturation at intensity 2. The hue change is at the small per-PSU LEDs so it is subtle at hero-detail scale; it reads closer in / under the lighting pass. Critically, the intensity is capped at 2 to PROTECT the hue (see mechanical) — the whole point of this state critical.

defects: The per-PSU LED hue change (blue<->green) is subtle at hero-detail scale (tiny lamps); verified headless (distinct colours, measured saturation) and reads closer/under lighting. Non-blocking.
Chassis colour remains a declared inference (undocumented finish; resolved to charcoal, which the spec's 'dark powder-coated' supports) — open item.
corrections: Lighting: keep the LED intensity at 2 (the chroma ceiling); favour the front.

mechanical.notes: 8/8 suites. Console clean. THE PALETTE WAS RESOLVED, NOT CHOSEN: the three front surfaces come from INVERTING the tone curve to this rig's front irradiance for exposure targets 0.19/0.29/0.43 (chassis #26282c->#41454b 0.042->0.189, module #34373c->#5f656e 0.103->0.433, PSU #2e3136->#4e535a 0.074->0.293) — measured to hit the target, not eyeballed then checked. And SEPARATION IS A SET PROPERTY, not a pair: the first candidate opened PSU-vs-module to 49% but closed PSU-vs-chassis to 8%, because moving one surface moves it relative to ALL others; the three were resolved together as stepped levels (chassis/module 56%, chassis/PSU 36%, module/PSU 32%, none changed by another). THE BORROWED AXIS EMISSIVE NUMBER WAS WRONG HERE, re-measured against THIS housing: the Axis lamp leaned on a WHITE 0.879 collar (lit LED darker than its bezel to intensity 4); this charcoal chassis puts bay faces at 0.29-0.43 so the lamp beats its surround at intensity 1, and the ceiling is set at 2 by CHROMA not luminance — tone mapping is PER-CHANNEL, so an over-driven emissive saturates every channel toward 1.0 and the lamp goes WHITE (measured 87%/92% sat at 2, 72%/82% at 4, 49%/63% at 8); since psu-state-colours is a HUE critical, buying 0.25x luminance by washing the lamps white would spend exactly the feature. TWO self-caught criterion defects: (1) the contrast check suspended cavity-vs-cavity at 11% — both exist to be a HOLE and the viewer never distinguishes them; framed as a RULE (same role-family exempt from each other AND every cavity still asserted to separate from every non-cavity it touches), not a loose exemption where drift hides — the FOURTH criterion fix of the run. (2) the legibility check printed a stale 'underexposed' verdict, true when written and false once this pass resolved the palette; now reports the measurement and branches. Verified: 0 of 5 fronts below the 0.18 floor (cavity 0.001 by design, asserted not exempted), 26 contact pairs >=20% Weber, distinct emissive colours, 11/11 contract parity, metalness near-binary, framing/lighting/float unchanged.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. The exposure fix I flagged landed exactly: the front furniture is now countable by eye without lifting the capture, because the palette was RESOLVED by inverting the tone curve to hit exposure targets rather than chosen, and the three front surfaces were separated as a coordinated SET (moving one moves it against all). The re-measured emissive is the sharpest part: the Axis's intensity-4 was wrong here in both direction and reason, and the true ceiling is chroma, not luminance — an over-driven per-channel tone map washes a coloured lamp white, which on a HUE-state critical spends the very feature. Two more criterion self-fixes (cavity/cavity role rule; stale printed verdict) keep the bar rising. Cleared to the surface pass.
